topic: Donation tax credit (federal, 2025): 14.5% on the first $200 of gifts, 29% above $200 (33% part for taxable income above $253,414); you or your spouse/common-law partner may claim gifts; unused amounts carry forward up to 5 years

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Alex and Sam each give $200 to registered charities in 2025; separately 200 x 14.5% = $29 each ($58); on one return 200 x 14.5% + 200 x 29% = $29 + $58 = $87; federal only, provincial credits add more and differ; assumes enough tax to absorb the credit and taxable income below $253,414. Carry-forward visual: two small gifts of $150 in different years claimed together (illustration).

sources.rates: canada.ca Report on Federal Tax Expenditures 2026 (Finance Canada): 2025 charitable donation credit 14.5% on the first $200, 29% above, 33% above $253,414 of taxable income; CRA 5000-G 2025 (lowest rate 14.5% for 2025) (via search 2026-10-31)
sources.who: canada.ca line 34900 'Who can claim': you or your spouse or common-law partner can claim eligible gifts (official receipts)
sources.carry: canada.ca line 34900 'How much you can claim': unused donations can be carried forward up to 5 years; carried-forward amounts are claimed first; generally limited to 75% of net income
